simple.meaning: מַעֲמָד (maʻămâd) is a Hebrew object word meaning “(figuratively) a position.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 1 Kings 10:5. The surrounding context includes family, family line, commandment, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַעֲמָד (H4612) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: מַעֲמָד (maʻămâd) / H4612 is traced through 1 Kings 10:5, 1 Chronicles 23:28, 2 Chronicles 9:4, 2 Chronicles 35:15 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H4612. maamad [ מַעֲמָד ] noun [masculine] office, function, service ; — 1 station, office, post ( מַעֲמָֽדְךָ ) Isa 22:19 (|| מַצָּֽבְךָ ), עַלמַֿעֲמָדָם 2Chr 35:15 at their post . 2 office, function 1Chr 23:28 . 3 service , probably specifically waiting at table (strictly mode of standing ), construct מְשָֽׁרְתָיו מַעֲמַד 1Kin 10:5 2Chr 9:4 .
